question:
A 44-year-old woman presents with facial discomfort and nasal congestion lasting 10 days. Her
medical history is notable for chronic nasal congestion and anosmia, which have progressively
worsened over the past few years. She is otherwise healthy, without allergies, and is not on any
medications. On examination, her vital signs are normal, and she is afebrile. There is no tenderness
over the sinuses on palpation. Anterior rhinoscopy reveals bilateral lobulated masses with pale mucosa
in both nasal cavities. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) MRI with contrast of the sinuses (B) CT of the sinuses (C) Oral antibiotic therapy (D)
Allergy testing (E) Nasal decongestant spray (F) Referral to ENT specialist (G) Saline nasal irrigation
(H) Oral antihistamine therapy (I) Endoscopic biopsy of the masses (J) Intranasal glucocorticoid spray
 A. Nasal decongestant spray
B. Allergy testing
C. Oral antibiotic therapy
D. Saline nasal irrigation
E. Oral antihistamine therapy
F. Referral to ENT specialist
G. CT of the sinuses
H. MRI with contrast of the sinuses
I. Intranasal glucocorticoid spray
J. Endoscopic biopsy of the masses
